title: Factorise a difference of two squares and check all integer factor pairs
content: When a proof-by-contradiction question gives an equation of the form (linear expression)^2 - (linear expression)^2 = N for a fixed integer N, factorise the left-hand side as a difference of two squares: (A+B)(A-B) = N. If the unknowns are assumed to be positive integers, then A+B and A-B must themselves be a pair of positive integer factors of N whose product is N. List every such factor pair of N (you can discard any pair that would force a variable to be negative or non-integer given the constraints of the problem), set up the resulting pair of simultaneous linear equations for each pair in turn, and solve each one. If none of the factor pairs produces integer (or positive integer) solutions for the original unknowns, this is the contradiction that completes the proof.
